recall_prompt: Say how you would count the bijections from a seven-element set onto itself — what a bijection is as a count, and the number.
insider_note: The first mark is the sentence, not the number: a bijection uses each of the 7 images exactly once, so it is an arrangement of all 7 and the count is 7!. Then 7! = 5040 — the 720 answer is 6!, one factor short.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: A bijection is an arrangement of all 7
steps.margin_note: First mark. A bijection from A onto A pairs each element with a different element and uses all 7 — an arrangement of the 7 elements: ⁷P₇ = 7!.
lines: A bijection from A onto A gives the 7 elements
7 different images, all of A used:

recall.must_convey: That a bijection of a 7-element set onto itself is an arrangement of all 7 elements, counted by 7 factorial.
accept: a bijection onto itself is a rearrangement of the seven elements so it is seven factorial
one to one and onto, all seven images different, seven P seven which is seven factorial
bijection ante seven elements ni arrange cheyadam, seven factorial
n P n equals n factorial with n seven

steps.why: One-one and onto together mean every element of A is the image of exactly one element, so the map is a rearrangement of A. Rearrangements of n things are n!.
common_mistakes: Answering 7⁷ — that counts all functions, most of which are not bijections.
Answering 1, thinking only the identity map works.

steps.label: Evaluate 7!

accept: seven factorial is five thousand forty
seven into six into five into four into three into two into one is five thousand and forty
the answer is five thousand forty

steps.why: ⁿPₙ = n!/0! = n!; the number is the answer, not the symbol.
